_comment: Clear lead crystal: lead-oxide glass (24-30 % PbO), cast or cut and polished, the glass of decanters, tumblers, bowls and chandelier drops. TRANSLUCENTTHICK, unlike a pane (Glass_Clear is Thin): crystal is a solid, heavy body seen through, and what makes it crystal and not ordinary glass is its higher IOR (about 1.56 against soda-lime's 1.52), so it bends what is seen through it more and its facets throw brighter reflections. Param-only: a clear glass has no albedo texture. Physically Based has no lead-crystal entry, so the values are judgement. APPROXIMATE: dispersion, the rainbow fire of cut crystal, is not carried. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage), dust as a deposit (Phase10), fingerprints (handled glassware), gated by the Grime mask. Water spots would be a fourth; per C3 that is a sibling article. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: LeadCrystal_Clear_Clean_Base_s01_v01

sources.why: Physically Based has no lead-crystal entry. specular_ior 1.56, the refractive index of full lead crystal (about 24-30 % PbO; 1.545-1.57). base_color 1, roughness 0 and transmission 1 for a clear, polished glass, as Physically Based gives for its soda-lime and borosilicate glasses. transmission_color 0.98, 0.98, 0.97 at a 0.1 m path (transmission_depth): crystal is very nearly colourless, with a faint warm-grey cast in a thick piece; a tumbler's 5-10 cm of glass reads clear.
